purpose: Debt record, not approval. Each entry is a paper whose SHA256SUMS no longer describes its own files. Recorded so that CI can fail on NEW drift without first turning red on drift that predates the check.
how_this_was_found: content_binding_coverage exits 1 on the live tree, but every test of it used synthetic fixtures, so nothing ran it against the repository. The digest gate was reporting a failure no CI job read.
not_to_be_regenerated: Refreshing a manifest to match drifted content while retaining current-package authority deletes the evidence that content moved. Entries leave only after a real rebuild or an explicit SUPERSEDED reconciliation that retains the historical render closure and denies current submission authority; never by an unqualified hash-only rewrite.

papers/orion-11-recursive-epistemic-reco.note: one bound file's bytes differ from its digest: experiments/r4-faithful-comparator-v1/run_orion11_r4_faithful_comparator.py

papers/orion-12-open-world-scientific-di.note: no bytes drifted; journal_package/current_revision/SHA256SUMS pins a manuscript.pdf that is absent, and whose digest does not match the parent package's manuscript.pdf, so it names an earlier render not present on main

papers/orion-13-global-knowledge-portrai.note: no bytes drifted; journal_package/wave1_current/SHA256SUMS pins a manuscript.pdf that is absent, and whose digest does not match the parent package's manuscript.pdf, so it names an earlier render not present on main

papers/orion-20-structured-problem-solvi.note: six bound files differ from their digests: P10_ACTIVE_CLAIM_AUTHORITY_V1.json, manuscript/main.tex, manuscript/main.pdf and sections 02, 11 and 16

why_this_was_empty: The ratchet shipped with an empty papers map while the tree carried drift, so every drifted paper read as new and the test could never pass. Populating it with the drift that predates the check is what the record is for; no digest was regenerated and no drifted byte was touched.
